newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-ENGLAND CAPTAIN UNHAPPY DESPITE COMFORTABLE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLAND CAPTAIN UNHAPPY DESPITE COMFORTABLE WIN.

text.p: England crushed the United Arab Emirates 5-0 on Friday to advance to the second round of the world youth soccer championships but captain John Curtis said he was unhappy with his team's play.
"We didn't play very well and the Emirates put up a good fight," Curtis said. "We didn't expect them to be as good as they were."
Danny Murphy scored twice in the first half but the UAE defence foiled most of the England attacks.
By the second half England were well in control, with Murphy completing the tournament's first hat-trick. His goals came in the seventh, 34th and 49th minutes.
Michael Owen made it 4-0 in the 51st minute before an own goal by UAE defender Ali Al Yarees in the 59th minute completed the scoreline.
The win put England top of Group F on six points, two points ahead of second-placed Mexico, who also beat the UAE 5-0 in their opening match but were held to a 1-1 draw by Ivory Coast on Friday.
Argentina took first place in Group E by edging Canada 2-1 while Japan became the first Asian side to score a win in the tournament by beating Costa Rica 6-2.
